title: Spatial Auditing
text:
Example using the Ward of Ardwick in the Local Authority (LA) of Manchester shown as the thin black line in the map below. Ward has been chosen as it is a lot smaller than LA, but large enough for a meaningful analysis.
In this example the assessment will be carried out at Lower Super Output Area (LSOA). This is the spatial level that the census is carried out at and it is also the highest resolution population data that is available open access from the government. Indicies of Multiple Deprevation (IMD) statistics are also released annually at this spatial resolution.
The map below shows the LSOAs within Ardwick, coloured by the IMD rank in the country (out of 33755, lower is more deprived). Data for the audit will be imported for a 1km radius from the border of each LSOA. This is shown as the thicker black line.
For this example the following data will be used as the measure of play spaces:
OS data was downloaded from the portal and OSM data imported using the osmdata R package imported and trimed to the area.
Importing road collisions from the STATS19 national police database for the last 5 years (2020 to 2024) using the STATS19 R package.

title: Spatial Auditing
text:
Scoring
For the area within each LSOA and 1km from the border, the total area of play spaces is calculated along with the total collisions.
An example below is shown for LSOA Manchester 020E, which ranks in the 2% of most deprived areas in Great Britain.
The border of the LSOA is shown as the thick black line. The collisions and play facilities are trimmed to the 1km radius from the border of the LSOA and the total collisions and play area in km2 summed up.








In total this LSOA has 0.67km2 of “play” space and 96 killed or seriously (KSI) casualties.
Applying this to all LSOAs and applying a scoring system to the values.
The scoring for each LSOA is based on the IMD scale of 1-10, so play area and crashes scored on a scale of 1-10 by taking the max value of each and splitting it into 10 even levels from 0, where 10 is the best (IMD, lowest deprivation, crashes, the least crashes and play the highest play space).






For LSOA areas population data is available for every age and sex.














Weighted summary by age and sex for the entire ward of Ardwick. In this area there are 1493 Boys age 14 to 18 and the weighted mean score is 14.9.

text:
These tabs describe a method for assessing an area at LSOA level for:

number of KSI collisions
Index of Multiple Deprivation

Tab “Spatial Method” describes the methodology for the Ward of Ardwick
This method is applied to the Local Authority of Manchester, with the scores shown in the table “Manchester scores table” and plotted “Manchester scores map” and “Manchester population map” with the population of Under 18s dissagregated by age band and sex.
